answer: Sybil resistance rests on a per-identity copper bond: each new address must stake an amount sized to what it can withdraw in one window, and every stake is slashed for proven collusion. Running a thousand fakes costs a thousand stakes while per-identity reward stays flat, so cloning gains nothing. A shared orchard of wallets fails too, because the bond graph is public and one funded parent links all its children, forfeiting as one glacier of frozen capital. Cost grows linearly; payoff does not.
